medium-at180.label: Medium grid: wake development through 180 s

referenceContext.interpretation: Primary paper fits are context, not an exact matching-domain or automatic pass threshold. Its reported Nu fit spread is below 5%. Its domain is 25D upstream, 75D downstream, width 50D; ours is 32D in each streamwise direction and width 64D. Its Newtonian model also decouples constant-property flow and temperature. No Bn>0 table value is used.

definitions.forceCoefficients: C=2*(native F/rho)/(U^2 D), U=1 m/s, nominal D=2 m.
definitions.Nu: -native outward wall diffusion/(pi alpha DeltaT), alpha=.02 m^2/s, DeltaT=1 K. Nominal circular perimeter is used for literature normalization of the actual 128-sided wall flux.
definitions.cycles: Positive Cl zero crossings with linear interpolation; complete-cycle means and second moments use trapezoidal integration of native samples. No stationary state is inferred from a completed process or a single cycle.
definitions.scope: Native output postprocessing only; no rebuilt equation, cross-mesh field remap, new residual gate, or claim of mesh independence.

timeComparison.scope: Only maximum time step differs after the same exact native checkpoint. Global signal/field differences include accumulated phase and amplitude effects. These finite-window differences are not a proven global error bound. Developing cycles are not automatically treated as stationary.

interpretation.development: Both completed medium trajectories have small latest-cycle drift: lift RMS changes by .07558%/.06798% at maximum dt .05/.025. Do not extend these baselines to chase insignificant cycle tails.

timeControl.assessment: Persistent timestep amplitude/frequency effects remain after cycle drift is small. Instantaneous fields, phase and mean heat transfer must be assessed separately; local defect acceptance is not a global error guarantee.

interpretation.nextEvidence: Paused after closing the running 120 s fine-grid segment, as requested by the user. The queued 120-to-180 s extension never started. Resume only on explicit user instruction; developed fine-grid comparison at 180 s and final maturity qualification remain unfinished.
interpretation.fieldNorm: Global area RMS includes the large farfield and must not replace maximum or wake-local differences.
interpretation.reference: Literature fits use a different domain and remain context only; no automatic physical-qualification threshold.

threeTimeControl.assessment: Observed three-step differences and cycle drift are reported separately. Adjacent differences and log-ratio orders do not establish an asymptotic global error bound. Phase-aligned cycle amplitudes do not replace instantaneous field or accumulated phase assessment.

meshAt120.assessment: Each own last complete cycle uses identical post-startup controls. Latest-cycle lift RMS still changes by 2.657%/2.338% on the medium/fine meshes, comparable to their 2.566% difference; mean heat transfer is also still developing. The two-mesh differences therefore cannot be treated as fully developed spatial error. Actual adaptive time grids and demonstrated BE time sensitivity remain separate; no mesh-independence or general wall-heat-flux qualification.

verification.newTests: No solver/frontend change in this round; completed native results, input chains and declared control equality were checked. No unrelated or platform regression repeated.

limitations: Medium trajectories exhibit material maximum-step sensitivity in amplitude and phase; the native local BE error gate alone is not a long-time accuracy qualification.
Fine-grid evidence ends at 120 s. The planned 180 s fine-grid comparison remains uncompleted and was not counted as passing.
Two spatial levels do not establish mesh independence.
Reported observed temporal orders are finite three-step statistics, not proof of an asymptotic regime, a global error upper bound or local wall-heat-flux qualification.
No change to physical scope or default controls.
Reported process times include concurrent background load.

developingMeshComparison.interpretation: These are the two declared wall/wake meshes under identical post-startup controls. Actual adaptive time grids and startup pressure backends are reported separately. Own last complete cycles are phase-aligned only for plotting; development changes and time-step error must be assessed before interpreting differences as spatial accuracy. Two levels do not prove asymptotic mesh convergence. No cross-mesh field interpolation or independent equation audit is performed.

interpretation: All branches begin at the same exact accepted state and differ only in maximum dt.
Observed order is log2 of adjacent differences, not a proven asymptotic error bound or extrapolated accepted field.
Field differences include accumulated phase; the direction cosine helps describe whether adjacent field differences are aligned.
Global area RMS includes the large farfield and must not replace maximum/wake-local differences.
Cycle statistics use corresponding complete cycle ordinals after the shared start; phase is also reported without alignment.
No automatic accuracy or stationary-state threshold is introduced.
Wake-region RMS supplements the whole-domain norm; its stated geometric window is a reporting choice, not an accuracy gate.
